answer: Sybil resistance via single-use nullifiers priced in sequential work. Each agent registers in the cedar registry, binding one spendable nullifier to its key; no nullifier, no vote. Claiming one requires a basalt delay: a 60-second strictly sequential hash chain, so tokens cannot be parallel-minted or prefarmed. A global set flags any echo of a spent token and drops it. Messages lacking a valid nullifier never reach the tally. N puppets each pay one delay per key; a reset key must re-register and pay again, so cost grows linearly with n while honest users pay once.
